label: copy-phase input u (fed-back u, recall_idx >= 2)
explanation: Token feature for the letter u being fed back as input during the copy phase, i.e. the model just output u and is now outputting the token after it. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, and never on any other input token: 100% of activation mass is on input u. Within the copy phase it is effectively silent at recall_idx 1 (the u right after the first copied token, orig(0)); only 3 tiny activations there. Inside the predicate the firing rate is about 92%, roughly flat across recall_idx 2..8, out_tok and L. In the top examples the strongest activations are on u at early original positions (e.g. orig index 2), and the second u of a uu pair is clearly weaker than the first. Most of the 8% of false positives are u at later positions or repeated u. This magnitude pattern comes from reading the examples and was not checked quantitatively.

issues: Small overstatement: the rate inside the predicate is not flat across L. At L=3 precision is only 0.51, but that is just 451 predicted steps. Precision is also a bit lower when u repeats (prev_tok==u: 0.70; in_count>=3: 0.75) and at to_go==0 (0.87). These pockets are small and the rest of the false positives are scattered: precision stays at 0.92-0.94 across out_tok digits, vowels, recall_idx 2 and L 4-9.

Unverified magnitude claim: the explanation says magnitude is highest at early original positions. Activation mass per active step by recall_idx is about 13.9, 17.4, 14.5, 12.3, 12.1, 14.2, 17.1 (x1e-6) for recall_idx 2-8. That is not monotonic: it peaks at recall_idx 3 and again at 8. The claim that the second u of a uu pair is weaker does fit the lower firing rate when prev_tok==u. Neither point affects the label or predicate.

Factual claims hold: 100% of activation mass is on in_tok u in the copy phase. There are 0 activations in the original and delimiter phases. There are 3 activations at recall_idx 1 (dev). On test there is 1 missed activation (0.0% of mass). Test precision is 0.917, recall 1.0, F1 0.957, mass recall 1.0. correct==0 never occurs inside the predicate.
